S073-01.notes: Subject 'research' is singular and the narrative is past tense, so 'helped'. 'help'/'have helped' fail agreement; 'helping' leaves the relative clause without a finite verb. Facts check out: Drew was medical director of Blood for Britain (1940) and directed the American Red Cross pilot blood bank in 1941.

S073-02.notes: Items in the list contain internal commas, so they must be separated by semicolons, matching the later ';'. Comma is ambiguous; a colon can't follow the colon already after 'three ways'; no punctuation gives a fused list. Matches Catania's findings (electrolocation, stunning volleys, doublets that make prey twitch).

S073-03.notes: Singular subject 'spray' and present tense, so 'is'. The spray reaches about 100 C, so 'nearly as hot as boiling water' is accurate and the aiming claim is accurate.

S073-04.notes: There are two independent clauses. A and D are comma splices and C is a run-on. B uses a semicolon plus a comma after the conjunctive adverb.

S073-05.notes: Parallel series 'carry ... feed ... and then discard'. Every other option breaks the parallelism. Elaiosome myrmecochory in trilliums and bloodroot is accurate.

flags.note: The antecedent of 'that' is ambiguous. 'a bacterium, Vibrio fischeri, that lives inside a special organ' is a natural, grammatical reading: the relative clause attaches to the nearest noun, 'a bacterium', after the comma-set appositive, and it is factually true. 'colonies ... that live' is also grammatical. A and C are both defensible. Fix by rewriting so only one antecedent is possible, for example 'colonies of the bacterium Vibrio fischeri that ______' with no appositive commas (still ambiguous), or better 'light produced by Vibrio fischeri bacteria, which ______ inside...' so that only the plural works.

S073-06.notes: Probably keyed as C (colonies live), but A (bacterium lives) is equally defensible. Counter-illumination facts are accurate.

S073-07.notes: The pronoun refers back to 'round trip' (singular), so 'that of any other animal'. 'those' and 'the ones' are plural; 'it of' is ungrammatical. About 70,000 km a year (Egevang et al. 2010) and 'longest known' are standard claims.

S073-08.notes: Savage is the object of 'regarded' ('many artists regarded her as their mentor'), so 'whom'. 'who' is the intended trap, 'which' is wrong for a person, and 'whose' is ungrammatical here. The 1932 studio and her role as first director of the Harlem Community Art Center (1937) are accurate.

S073-09.notes: Plural subject 'sales', past narrative, so 'were'. The 'sheet music' attractor tempts 'was'. The one-cent royalty arranged with John Stark is accurate.

S073-10.notes: This is an indirect question, so it ends with a period. A wrongly uses a question mark, B has a stray closing quote, and D ends the sentence with a comma.

S073-11.notes: The colon explanation (features shown 'without softening', injuries depicted) supports 'rarely idealized'. 'rarely candid' and 'rarely personal' contradict it, and 'symbolic' is unsupported. About 55 self-portraits is the commonly cited figure.

S073-12.notes: 'Most earlier artists ... instead' signals a departure, so 'unconventional'. This is consistent with art-historical accounts of Lewis's 1876 Centennial piece.

S073-13.notes: The text moves from prediction to doubts to confirmation. Darwin 1862 and Xanthopan morganii praedicta described in 1903 are accurate. The wrong choices are clearly off.

S073-14.notes: 'also played a role' and 'sped up the drying that was already under way' mean Wright accepts the orbital cause and adds people as accelerants. B's 'sole cause' contradicts 'also'. The roughly 11,000 to 5,000 years ago dating and Wright's 2017 hypothesis are accurately represented.

flags.note: The passage never says outright that a signature raised prices; A depends on linking 'as collectors' interest grew' to signing. B ('take credit') is a tempting surface reading of signing other people's pots. The collector context makes A best, but one added clause (for example, that signed pots sold for more) would make the inference firmer.

S073-15.notes: A is best supported by the collector-interest framing. B attributes an unsupported self-serving motive, C is extreme, and D is unsupported. The 1918 development and 1920s signing are accurate, and historically she signed others' pots to help them sell.

S073-16.notes: Checked the numbers: 0, 2, 5 months correspond to 6, 18, 42 krill per cubic meter, a monotonic increase that matches the data. A and C give single points and D is not data.

S073-17.notes: The hypothesis is about the mechanism (shade). Shade cloth matching nurse-plant survival isolates shade as the factor. D shows only a nurse effect without the mechanism, which makes it the strong trap. A and B are irrelevant. Nurse-plant facts are accurate.

S073-18.notes: The text contrasts dominance and privileges with fading power, so 'However'. The Lübeck, Hamburg, London (Steelyard) and Bergen kontor details and the decline by the 1500s are accurate.

S073-19.notes: Working color by color across all panels leads to visual unity, a cause-and-effect relationship. The 1940-41 dates, 60 panels and color-by-color method are accurate.

S073-20.notes: Only C gives both the 1965 proposal and the 1999 board citation. B lacks the original proposal. D compares the wrong dates and never mentions the board's recognition. Checked 1999 - 1974 = 25, and the 1965 board refusal is accurate.

S073-21.notes: C defines Cepheids for an unfamiliar audience and states the significance (measuring distances). A and B give no significance, and D is about Hubble rather than Leavitt's discovery. The 1912 period-luminosity relation is accurate.
